title: UNFURLING VOICE
territory: A folded inward thought opens into a broad, speaking form: substantial ink, a held left root, and one clear release toward the right.
oneSentenceMeaning: A thought opens into speech while keeping the fold it came from.
appIdentity: Mluva gives a spoken thought somewhere useful to go. Its Czech name means speech or manner of speaking; its daily role is open-source dictation and rewriting for Omarchy. A shortcut, a sentence, and an editable draft should feel immediate and quietly satisfying. The identity should hold the confidence of a practical desktop tool together with the small pleasure of expressing something clearly. Its promise, Most delightful dictation for Omarchy, is an ambition about the experience; A little more delight every day gives that ambition a human scale. The product retains original recognition beside working versions and completed rewrites, with precise, editable Markdown available for further work. Speech and rewrite providers can be local or cloud, chosen independently. The mark therefore communicates expression and continuity. It makes no inference-location, privacy, accuracy, or automatic-delivery promise.
markIdentity: The initial mark is a thought caught at the instant it opens. Two broad, unequal filled forms share an implied hinge on the left. The upper form has lifted and extended outward; the smaller lower form still holds the original compact posture. A widening interval of transparent space gives the opening a direction and makes the relationship explainable without animation. Petal and mouth are useful physical starting points because both open through a change in posture. The finished identity needs the compression and release of that action, with no botanical anatomy or literal lips. Its character is generous, composed, and a little unexpected. The dense parts should look deliberately cut and shaped, with enough mass for a small panel icon. The lower fold also offers an understated connection to Mluva's retained source: expression can change shape while its starting point remains present.
logoDescription:
The initial design uses two substantial solid shapes, a lifted upper fold and a compact lower fold, arranged across a horizontal axis that rises gently toward the right. The combined footprint is slightly wider than tall, roughly five units wide to four high. Both pieces have broad surfaces and changing thickness. They must never collapse into two curved lines or a pair of pointed leaves.

The upper piece carries about two thirds of the ink. Its left end is full and tucked inward, as if it has just released from a compact fold. The top boundary lifts through one generous curve into a broad shoulder. The right end turns down softly and finishes with a blunt, almost vertical face. Its underside returns toward the left in a much tighter curve. This difference between a leisurely outer edge and a gathered inner edge supplies the sense of a surface opening without any drawn seam, highlight, or paper effect.

The lower piece is shorter and heavier toward the left. Its underside settles into a quiet base; its upper edge rises slightly toward a thick terminal that stops well before the upper piece's farthest reach. The two left ends sit close enough to imply a common origin, but remain separated by actual transparency. The interval between them widens decisively toward the right. That open interval is the main event: the viewer should be able to point to it and say that something held inside has opened.

The silhouette should carry a faint mouthlike presence without being a pair of lips. Avoid bilateral symmetry, a pointed beak, a central seed, veins, radial repetition, or a dangling tail. Keep the two pieces unequal in length, mass, and curvature. Use one fully opaque ink color on actual transparent alpha. A small mark should still register as a compact thing unfolding; the same geometry at film-title size should reveal the controlled change in curvature. The initial study deliberately tests whether the implied hinge can hold the parts together perceptually before the revision decides whether a continuous form is stronger.
wordmarkDescription:
The initial wordmark spells exactly Mluva: one capital M followed by lowercase l, u, v, and a. Start from JetBrains Mono Medium as outlined letter geometry, keeping its practical rhythm, recognizable constructions, and comfortable counters. This connects the name with the app's editable text and Omarchy setting. Optical spacing may depart from monospacing; the letters should still feel related to the bundled family.

Give the capital M a little extra width and deepen its inner valley so its diagonals seem to open from a firm pair of uprights. Soften only the deepest point of that valley. The M remains a readable capital, with no detached diagonals or decorative notch. Narrow the l substantially while retaining a clear top entry and a short foot. Let that foot turn outward with a broad corner, as though a compact vertical form has begun to open. These two edits establish a clear beginning to the name.

The u initially carries the most direct echo of the mark. Shift its bowl slightly toward the right, make the bottom more generous, and let the right stem end with a shallow outward cut. Keep a broad clear counter and enough straight stem to preserve the letter. Continue the same opening angle into the terminal of the v and the exit of the a, but retain the v's pointed internal junction and the a's double-storey construction. The name should remain readable before anyone discovers these correspondences.

Balance M–l, l–u, u–v, and v–a by visible white space rather than equal numerical gaps. The narrow l should relieve density after the capital without creating a break that looks like two words. Use solid filled contours, one ink color, and no symbol beside the lettering. The initial question is whether distributing the opening gesture across several terminals gives the word a coherent character or introduces too many competing details. The revision must choose a smaller set of changes that stays obvious at ordinary title sizes.
selfCritique: The two-piece initial mark can read as a clam, a pair of leaves, or two unrelated organic blobs. Calling their gap a hinge does not make a hinge visible. The revision should create a continuous left root so one thing is visibly opening.

An upper and lower shape around a horizontal gap can become cosmetic lips or a messaging mouth. Different lengths help, but the design also needs an oblique opening, an unequal vertical distribution of mass, and broad blunt ends.

The petal metaphor is easy to overdraw into a wellness identity. Any pointed tip, stem, vein, radial arrangement, or symmetrical botanical proportion should be removed. The useful idea is the act of opening.

Joining the pieces solves their weak relationship but creates a new risk: a generic chunky C, crescent, or bitten disc. The upper shoulder must have its own oblique direction, and the short lower return must end inside the silhouette rather than mirror the upper tip.

A narrow throat could disappear at 24 px and leave an unexplained blob. A wide throat could empty the mark into an outline. The opening and the surrounding mass must both receive explicit minimum proportions.

The first wordmark edits almost every letter. Repeated diagonal terminal cuts can resemble a technology stencil treatment and weaken the calm quality of JetBrains Mono. Concentrate authorship in the M, l, and u; let v and a do their normal reading work.

An exaggerated u bowl can read as a smile, and a flamboyant l foot can become a hook. Neither needs to act out the whole logo. Their changes should be structural enough to notice, with familiar letter skeletons and no swashes.

The explanation about retained source is a useful secondary association, but a viewer cannot infer version integrity or provider behavior from a fold. Product copy must carry those facts. The mark only has to make opening into expression discussable.
revision:
The revised final mark is one continuous filled form. Join the two initial pieces through a broad left heel and remove the separating root slit. The held origin is now visible in the silhouette. A deep, open bay enters from the right and turns gently inward, separating a tall upper canopy from a short lower return. Use a footprint of approximately 100 units wide by 82 high. The upper canopy reaches the farthest right point; the lower return stops near 76 units. Their unequal reach makes the opening directional even when the mark is still.

Give the upper canopy a long, gently rising shoulder followed by one generous convex turn into a broad, softly squared terminal. The upper mass should feel like a heavy surface released outward. The lower return is compact, with a settled underside and a blunt oblique end. It turns only enough to register a fold; it must not curl into a spiral. The bay points about twelve degrees above horizontal. Its deepest visible passage stays at least twelve units wide, its back ends in an open rounded elbow, and it contains no enclosed counter. Keep the heel about twenty-eight units thick and each projecting mass at least twenty units thick. These are construction targets for optical review, not claims of completed pixel testing.

The final wordmark reduces the active changes to M, l, and u. Widen M about seven percent, deepen its valley to roughly two thirds of cap height measured from the top, and round only that valley's turn. Narrow l to about half the original advance, retain its top entry, and give its short right foot a broad lifted corner. Shift the u's bowl slightly right and open its counter modestly; its right terminal receives the same shallow rising cut as the mark's bay. Keep v and the double-storey a close to their original outlines, adjusting only weight and spacing. All five letters remain separate and upright.

The revised relationship is one unfolding silhouette beside one readable, intentionally sculpted name. The persistent risk is a C or shell reading. Reject executions whose upper and lower ends become equal, whose bay is a horizontal bite, or whose outer boundary becomes circular. The final prompts below describe only this revised geometry.

One continuous, substantial filled ink silhouette, flat monochrome near-black, on actual transparent alpha; all empty space and the canvas must be transparent. The symbol depicts a compact thought opening outward through its shape. Proportions about 100 wide by 82 high. A broad continuous left heel supports a tall upper canopy and a shorter lower return. A deep rounded bay enters from the right, opening about 12 degrees upward, with no enclosed hole. The tall upper mass extends to the farthest right point; its long gently rising shoulder turns through a generous convex curve into a broad softly squared terminal. The compact lower mass ends around 76 percent of the total width, with a quiet underside and a blunt oblique end. The upper and lower ends are visibly unequal. Preserve an inner passage at least 12 percent of the total width; keep the left heel about 28 percent of the width and the substantial projecting masses at least 20 percent thick. Dense silhouette, deliberate asymmetry, calm outward release, recognizable at 24 px. No stroked paths, outlines, thin crescents, radial petals, leaves, veins, page fold, lips, teeth, tongue, speech bubble, microphone, water blob, swirl, circle with a bite, copied brand, gradient, glow, texture, shadow, app tile, background rectangle, checkerboard artwork, labels, mockups, presentation board, or wordmark. Show exactly one standalone final symbol, centered with generous transparent margin.
wordmarkPrompt: Create wordmark lettering only. Render exactly Mluva, with capital M and lowercase luva, one word, no other text and no accompanying symbol. Start from JetBrains Mono Medium and visibly sculpt the outlines while preserving effortless reading. Solid flat monochrome near-black filled letters on actual transparent alpha; no opaque background or checkerboard artwork. Keep all five letters separate and upright. Widen M about seven percent, deepen its inner valley to about two thirds of cap height measured downward from the top, and give only the valley's turn a small soft radius; preserve clear outer uprights and diagonals. Narrow the lowercase l advance to about half the original, retain a recognizable top entry, and shape its short right foot with a broad lifted corner, no swash. Give u a slightly right-shifted generous bowl, an open counter, and a shallow twelve-degree rising cut at its right stem terminal. Keep v and the double-storey a close to JetBrains Mono, adjusting weight and optical spacing to harmonize. Maintain full-size counters, even apparent weight, and deliberate white space between M–l, l–u, u–v, and v–a. The visible signature is a firm open M, compact l, and softly opening u. No stencil gaps, ligatures, italic slant, handwritten styling, added icons, logo symbol, gradients, glow, outline treatment, shadows, labels, slogans, mockups, app tile, or presentation board. Show exactly one clean horizontal wordmark centered with generous transparent margins.
smallSizeRisks: At 24 px, the mark is evaluated within roughly 21 × 17 px of actual silhouette. The bay should retain about 2.5 px of separation at its narrowest useful passage; this remains a target until rendering is checked.
The joined left heel can become overweight and turn the mark into a block. Preserve its rounded inner elbow while keeping the exterior from becoming a circle.
The upper terminal may visually sag after downsampling. Lift its underside optically without thinning its mass or sharpening it into a leaf.
The lower return must remain a short substantial fold. If its tip stretches rightward, the symbol becomes lips or a symmetrical open shell.
Use the symbol alone at panel-icon sizes. The complete name needs enough height for the double-storey a and the narrowed l to remain distinct.
Reversed ink can appear heavier. Enlarge the bay slightly in a separately reviewed small reversed version only if actual raster evidence requires it.
opticalRules: Use a single filled path for the revised mark; no stroke, root slit, detached accent, enclosed counter, or supporting tile.
Keep the broad upper reach and short lower return unmistakably unequal; preserve the upward opening axis and avoid a circular exterior.
Treat 100:82 as the starting footprint, 12 percent of width as the minimum bay passage, and 20 percent as the minimum projecting mass; tune after a real 24 px reduction.
Maintain the apparent center by shifting the mark slightly right of its geometric center when necessary; assess the left heel's visual weight rather than centering its bounding box blindly.
Leave clear space of at least one quarter of mark height around standalone use. If a later lockup is tested, let the symbol align to the wordmark's optical body, with independent spacing.
Keep the M valley and u counter visibly open. Preserve the double-storey a, readable l top entry, and separate letter contours.
Set M–l and l–u by white-space balance after narrowing l. Do not preserve equal monospaced advances as a constraint.
Render fully opaque ink with genuine transparent alpha. Frost reversal is a separate color application of the same identity; gradients and partial fill opacity are outside this study.
motionRelationship: A later brand reveal can begin with a more compact bay and lift the upper canopy through a small opening rotation while the left heel and lower return remain settled. Stop on the exact final silhouette; avoid bouncing, elastic overshoot, or continuous morphing. The wordmark can appear as a single calm unit after the opening has become readable. Keep all letters intact throughout. This gesture can coexist with the film kit's water and existing 3.4-second breathing cadence, but the logo remains a solid, static identity asset and should not turn into the recorder's metaball light. Recording and finalization indicators must continue to communicate their own real states. A reduced-motion version presents the final mark and wordmark immediately. Any film reveal remains an authored identity treatment, with no implied provider latency or recognition progress.
